sources.title: M. Artin, Algebraic Geometry, Chapter 3 `Projective Varieties`
sources.locator: Complete 189-page MIT-hosted PDF; Chapter 3 contents and §§3.1–3.2, 3.4, printed pp. 58–72 / PDF pp. 61–75, read in full on 2026-09-05.

contents.name: §3.1, Segre product construction
contents.reason: The Segre map is the first construction of the later page devoted to products, Segre and Veronese embeddings, and Grassmannians; including it here would split its defining equations from the product theory it needs.

contents.name: Proposition 3.1.15, Veronese embedding
contents.reason: This embedding is assigned with the Segre construction to the later projective-geometry page, so its coordinate equations and geometric use are not duplicated before that page's prerequisite development.

contents.name: §3.2, quasiprojective varieties
contents.reason: Quasiprojective varieties require the separate open-subvariety and gluing development beyond this pair's decided projective-set, coordinate, cone, and homogeneous-morphism route; they are not a prerequisite of any scaffolded claim here.

contents.reason: The graph construction lives naturally with products and closed embeddings on the subsequent projective-geometry page; this pair only establishes homogeneous-coordinate maps and does not yet introduce the product ambient space.

sources.title: D. Arapura, Notes on Algebraic Geometry, Chapter 2 `Projective Varieties`
sources.locator: Complete 41-page author-hosted PDF; Chapter 2, §§2.1–2.5, PDF pp. 15–22, read in full on 2026-09-05.

contents.name: Lemma 2.2.2, compactness of complex projective space
contents.reason: This is a complex-analytic compactness statement, while this classical algebraic page works over the established algebraically closed field and deliberately postpones properness and analytic topology; it supplies no prerequisite used by the chosen route.

contents.name: Lemma 2.2.4, homogeneous ideals and affine cones
Theorem 2.2.5, projective Nullstellensatz and the irrelevant ideal
Theorem 2.3.3, closure as the projective zero locus of the homogenized ideal
Lemma 2.3.4, saturation of homogenized chosen generators
§2.4, Segre embedding
contents.reason: The plan gives the Segre embedding to the later page on products, Segre and Veronese embeddings, and Grassmannians, where product coordinates and its defining ideal will be authored as one coherent construction.

contents.name: §2.4, rational normal curve
contents.reason: This curve is the concrete Veronese example for the later embeddings page; this pair needs only the saturation counterexample and projective charts, so introducing the complete rational-normal-curve treatment here would duplicate that later scope.

contents.name: §2.5, Plücker coordinates and the Grassmannian
contents.reason: Plücker coordinates require the Grassmannian and exterior-coordinate construction that the designated later page owns; neither is required to establish projective algebraic sets, cones, or homogeneous-coordinate morphisms in this pair.
